text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate observed on /v1/decode (streaming) — 5xx spike, GPU OOMs detected on eu-west-1-decode-pool. Pager triggered at 2025-08-19T09:12:30Z :rotating_light:
maya (oncall): acked. joining. seeing lots of dropped requests in telemetry, can someone paste the recent error signatures?
kevin (eng-runtime): throwing CUDA out-of-memory in decode loop, stack shows `at runtime/decoder.cu:line 842` and continuous retries -> memory growth. logs attached to incident console.
sam (sre): looks like a token-spiral: clients sending long generation, `max_tokens` mismatch between SDK and route config. some requests end up unbounded.
maya (oncall): timeline? did any deploy just go out?
deploy-bot: deploy started by @kevin at 2025-08-19T08:59:10Z - rolling patch to batching scheduler (will complete 09:05Z).
kevin (eng-runtime): the patch shouldn't touch token caps but may change batch packing; could have exposed worst-case memory packing.
leah (support): we have 4 customer tickets reporting partial responses / dropped streams in last 20m (IDs 3421,3422,3425,3430) — high-severity. customers noticed mid-generation disconnects.
anton (customer-ops): flagged one affected customer on Dedicated who says their job was mid-run and got cut, asked for ETA and mitigation.
tess (product): what's immediate mitigation? we need a fallback for hosted + dedicated.
maya (oncall): immediate actions: 1) pause incoming streaming traffic to eu-west-1 decode pool by setting route weight 0 -> fallback, 2) scaleup fallback pool (cpu decode) + enable throttling, 3) quarantine suspicious client tokens. I'll run the route change.
kevin (eng-runtime): suggest also enforce server-side `max_tokens=1024` hard cap for all streaming decode requests in eu-west-1 for next 30m. I can push config via feature-flags.
sam (sre): I'll push a temporary admission control to drop requests with extremely long prompt+max_tokens combos (> 50k total seq). will emit 429 with reason.
maya (oncall): route change applied: eu-west-1 decode routing -> weight 0 to decode-gpu, weight 1 to decode-fallback-cpu. Monitoring.
deploy-bot: route update successfully propagated to control-plane (09:18:02Z).
kevin (eng-runtime): applying feature flag hard cap now: `ff.set('eu-west-1.decode.hard_max_tokens', 1024)`
kevin (eng-runtime): feature flag applied. Will also push a hotpatch to avoid kv-cache growth for partially completed streams.
leah (support): customer timeline update: told affected customers we are routing to fallback and rate-limiting, they might see slower but complete responses.
anton (customer-ops): negotiating an incident bridge with Dedicated customer — offering credits and a postmortem.
tess (product): ok please log all request ids for ones we dropped for later repro. prioritize any customer-provided prompts.
sam (sre): telemetry: OOMs dropped from ~18/min to 0/min after route change and caps. upstream 5xx rate back to baseline.
maya (oncall): confirming metrics: GPU memory usage on decode-pool fell to normal within 2 minutes of routing. KV-cache growth audits also show truncation working.
kevin (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: recent packing change allowed a small number of streaming sessions to accumulate very large KV cache due to missing max_tokens enforcement on server side; paired with a heavy model instance on a small GPU, it triggered heap exhaustion and container restarts.
sam (sre): container restarts observed on 3 nodes (eu-west-1-decode-03/07/11) between 09:10-09:14Z. Crash log snippet: `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::OutOfMemoryError'` then `CUDA error: out of memory`.
maya (oncall): mitigation summary: route diverted, hard cap applied, admission control, quarantined token list (w/ids) — are we confident it's safe to bring decode-gpu back or do we need a further change?
kevin (eng-runtime): we should roll back the recent packing change and add server-side trimming of in-progress KV caches for streaming sessions over threshold. rolling rollback to canary 2025-08-19T08:50 now.
deploy-bot: rollback started at 09:25:12Z.
leah (support): customer update: notified Dedicated customer that we applied a temporary cap and routed to fallback; they requested ETA to restore GPU path.
anton (customer-ops): they asked if data was lost. we confirmed partial streams for some requests; logs show final tokens not emitted for ~12 requests. customers want retention of those request ids for retries.
sam (sre): will surface list of impacted request ids to support.
kevin (eng-runtime): rollback complete at 09:31:00Z to canary. Reintroducing GPU routing in 10m with additional guardrails (server-side cap + KV trim).
maya (oncall): re-enable GPU routing in gradual increments. will monitor OOMs, set circuit-breaker to trip if OOMs >1 within 5m.
kevin (eng-runtime): added KV trim: streaming sessions truncates oldest KV entries when >256k tokens cached. pushed at 09:34Z.
sam (sre): circuit-breaker rule deployed.
maya (oncall): reenabled 10% weight to decode-gpu at 09:40Z. currently 0 OOMs, tail latency ok. raising to 30% at 09:44Z.
leah (support): support updated customers: gradual restore, credits offered, and we will run a targeted repro for impacted prompts.
tess (product): please add a checklist item to prevent SDK/route config drift for max_tokens — maybe server-side lint in the control plane.\eot
maya (oncall): handoff to night oncall @kevin at 10:00Z. full incident notes + actions: route diversion, hard cap, admission control, KV trimming, rollback packing change, gradual restore. Please produce a postmortem doc.
kevin (eng-runtime): acknowledged handoff, will create postmortem draft and include proposed permanent mitigations: server-side enforced caps, telemetry alert on KV growth, and symmetric config validation between SDK and route layer.
incident-bot: Incident severity: Sev2 -> Transitioning to Post-Incident Review state. Pager cleared at 10:02:18Z.
